content: Hijama, derived from the Arabic word حجامة meaning sucking, refers to the practice of wet cupping in traditional Arab medicine. This therapeutic procedure involves creating a vacuum to draw blood from small incisions made on the skin. Hijama is particularly significant among Muslims, as it is explicitly mentioned and encouraged in Islamic tradition by the Prophet Muhammad. For instance, in a hadith recorded by Imam Bukhari (5263) and Imam Muslim (2952), the Prophet is quoted as saying, Hijama is among your best remedies (خير ما تداويتم به الحجامة). Procedure Hijama is commonly performed on the head but can be applied to other areas of the body, especially at sites of pain or discomfort, to alleviate symptoms. A conservative approach, as outlined by the Broken Earth Cupping Site, advises against excessive cupping and suggests that targeting six specific points on the body is sufficient to cleanse the cardiovascular system. These points include the back of the head, the two shoulders corresponding to acupuncture heart positions, the lower back (tail area), and the two inner ankles. Before the procedure, the area may be shaved to ensure a tight seal with the cup. The cup, typically made of metal, glass, or plastic (though traditionally horns were used), is placed on the chosen site. In some cases, leeches may be used as an alternative. A vacuum seal is then created. Historically, this was achieved by burning a small piece of paper or cotton inside the cup, causing it to adhere to the skin. Modern methods, however, use a machine to create the vacuum. The cup is left in place for a few minutes before being removed, at which point small incisions are made in the skin. The cup is then reapplied to allow blood to fill it. Prophet Muhammad and Hijama Islamic tradition contains numerous hadiths supporting the practice of hijama. For example: Abu Kabsha al-Anmari reported that the Prophet performed cupping on his head and between his shoulders, stating, Whoever sheds some of this blood will experience no pain in not being treated for a certain disease with a certain cure. Anas provided a more anatomically precise account, noting that the Prophet cupped two different neck veins and the upper back. Jabir narrated that the Prophet also cupped his hip to relieve pain in that area. Abu Hurayra quoted the Prophet as saying, If there is good in one thing which cures you, it is cupping. Additionally, Abu Hurayra reported that the Prophet recommended cupping on the 17th, 19th, or 21st days of the lunar month, promising healing from every disease for those who follow this timing.
